names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 12 decembrie, «Sfântul Mucenic Sinet», with the rank word left off.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 12 Δεκεμβρίου, «Άγιος Συνετός», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 12. децембар ст. ст., „Свети мученик Разумник.“ — with «Свети» (“saint”) and «мученик» (the `martyr` grade `types` keeps) left off, which leaves the name the heading gives. IT IS THE SLAVONIC RENDERING AND NOT THE GREEK NAME, and the book says so itself in its first line: «Грчко му је име Синетос или Синезије», his Greek name is Synetos or Synesios. Those two are the book’s own Cyrillic spellings of a Greek name and were NOT drafted as forms of their own — the Greek «Συνετός» in this folder was read off a Greek page, and §6 and BRIEF.md §5 both forbid a reader to make a script form out of another book’s transcription. `sr-foldpred.mjs` measured the folded string at 0 other holders.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 12 decembrie — «Sfântul Mucenic Sinet»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 12ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιος Συνετός»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 12 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps, and the entry is the same man: the reader of the church of Rome who refused to sacrifice and was beheaded. **The page's two datings do not agree with each other**: it puts his martyrdom in the third century at Rome under Aurelian, whose reign was 270 to 275, and in the same breath makes him a reader appointed by Pope Xystus, whom the corpus keeps as `sixtus-ii-of-rome` and who died in 258 — and whom this page itself refers to 10 Αυγούστου. One of the two cannot stand, the page does not choose, and therefore **no `dates` object is proposed**; the difficulty is named in the report. The reader's appointment by Xystus is the page's statement and would be the ground of a `related` row, but because it is the half of the page that contradicts the other half, none is drafted and the matter is left to the author. No hymn is printed. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The corpus's `types` vocabulary has no word for a reader, so none is added; the office is left in the life where the page puts it.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 25.12.2025 (12. децембар ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Разумник.“

attestations.note: The day’s third and last entry, quoted whole with its closing full stop; URL year 2025. **THE HEADING NAMES HIM IN TRANSLATION AND THE BODY GIVES THE GREEK BACK**: «Грчко му је име Синетос или Синезије», his Greek name is Synetos or Synesios, where «Разумник» is the Slavonic rendering of it — the Intelligent — and that sentence is what identifies him beyond doubt as saint.gr’s «Άγιος Συνετός» and doxologia.ro’s «Sfântul Mucenic Sinet». The stored form is the heading’s «Разумник», §6 asking for the form the calendar prints: «Синетос» and «Синезије» are the book’s own Cyrillic renderings of a Greek name, not Greek-script forms, and the Greek form this folder already holds was read off a Greek page, so neither was drafted as a second form. `types` UNTOUCHED: «мученик» is the `martyr` held, and «чтец» — a reader — is a grade the corpus’s `types` vocabulary does not carry, so nothing was added for it and it is in the life instead. **`dates` DELIBERATELY STILL ABSENT**: the entry dates him only by a reign, «у време цара Аврелијана», in the days of the emperor Aurelian, and gives that reign no years; BRIEF.md §4 says that where the page gives no year there is no `dates` object, and the reign’s own dates are not on this page to be taken. NO `locations`: Rome is named and the folder has never held a coordinate. NO `related` row: the entry names nobody but the emperor. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
